extracted.intended_audience: medical, dental, and technical students and laboratory workers in bacteriology
extracted.subtask_description: Practical laboratory guidance for selection, preparation, sterilisation, cleaning, handling, and storage of glassware, apparatus, cultures, and infective materials in a bacteriological laboratory; includes safety/regulatory rules and detailed apparatus specifications and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 1: wearing gown/overall
rubrics_metrics.description: Each worker must wear a gown or overall, provided at his own expense, which must be kept in the Laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to prevent personal contamination and to ensure clothing reserved for laboratory use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 2: hand disinfection
rubrics_metrics.description: The hands must be disinfected with lysol 2 per cent. solution, carbolic acid 5 per cent. solution, or corrosive sublimate 1 per mille solution, after dealing with infectious material, and before using towels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies disinfectants and occasions (after handling infectious material; before using towels).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 3: towels/dusters not for infectious material
rubrics_metrics.description: On no account must Laboratory towels or dusters be used for wiping up infectious material, and if such towels or dusters do become soiled, they must be immediately sterilised by boiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids mechanical spread via cleaning cloths; requires immediate sterilisation by boiling if contaminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 4: disposal in disinfectant pails
rubrics_metrics.description: Special pails containing disinfectant are provided to receive any waste material, and nothing must be thrown on the floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All waste from infectious work must be placed in disinfectant receptacles rather than discarded indiscriminately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 5: immediate instrument disinfection
rubrics_metrics.description: All instruments must be flamed, boiled, or otherwise disinfected immediately after use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents cross-contamination by requiring prompt decontamination of tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 6: labels moistened with water
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels must be moistened with water, and not by the mouth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids risk of infection from mouth contact; enforces hygienic labeling practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 7: disposal of disused slides/cover-glasses/pipettes
rubrics_metrics.description: All disused cover-glasses, slides, and pipettes after use in handling infectious material, etc., must be placed in 2 per cent. lysol solution. A vessel is supplied on each bench for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bench-level provision for immediate chemical immersion of contaminated small glassware to reduce risk and allow later sterilisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 8: cultures placed for immediate disinfection
rubrics_metrics.description: All plate and tube cultures of pathogenic organisms when done with, must be placed for immediate disinfection in the boxes provided for the purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultures must not be left accessible; use designated boxes for disinfection right after use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 9: fluids must be disinfected before drains
rubrics_metrics.description: No fluids are to be discharged into sinks or drains unless previously disinfected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects plumbing and public health by requiring prior chemical or thermal inactivation of biological material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 10: animal dissection precautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals are to be dissected only after being nailed out on the wooden boards, and their skin thoroughly washed with disinfectant solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure reduces exposure and surface contamination during dissection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 11: cadaver handling after post-mortem
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately after the post-mortem examination is completed each cadaver must be placed in the zinc animal-box—without removing the carcase from the post-mortem board—and the cover of the box replaced, ready for carriage to the destructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimises handling and risk of environmental contamination; preserves containment until disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 12: cremation and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Dead animals, when done with, are cremated in the destructor, and the laboratory attendant must be notified when the bodies are ready for cremation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures proper disposal of infectious animal material and coordination with staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 13: restricted animal-house access
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the workers in the laboratory are allowed to enter the animal houses unless accompanied by the special attendant in charge, who must scrupulously observe the same directions regarding personal disinfection as the workers in the laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls access and enforces same disinfection standards for animal-house entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 14: no cultures removed without permission
rubrics_metrics.description: No cultures are to be taken out of the laboratory without the permission of the head of the Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents unauthorized transport of potentially pathogenic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation 15: report accidents immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: All accidents, such as spilling infected material, cutting or pricking the fingers, must be at once reported to the bacteriologist in charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures prompt response, treatment, and record of exposure incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test-tube selection and specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep several sizes of test-tubes in stock (e.g., 18 x 1.5 cm; 18 x 1.3 cm; 18 x 2 cm; 13 x 1.5 cm; 5 x 0.7 cm), made from the best German potash glass 'blue-lined', stout and heavy, with the mouth slightly turned over but not forming a rim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose robust, uniform tubes for reusability and safety; sort new supplies for consistent calibres to simplify ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flask selection (Bohemian, pear-shaped, Erlenmeyer, Kolle, Roux, Guy's)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a variety of flasks: Bohemian flasks (250–3000 c.c.), pear-shaped for small sizes, Erlenmeyer (75,100,250 c.c.) with narrow neck ~2 cm for culture flasks; Kolle's flat culture flasks for large surface areas; Roux bottles and Guy's culture bottle for narrow neck and deeper medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select flask shapes by intended use—surface area, prevention of contamination, stacking, and vigorous growth; prefer narrow necks to reduce contamination risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter/Kitasato serum flask requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter flasks or Kitasato's serum flasks in sizes 250 to 2000 c.c.; must be of stout glass to resist pressure and thoroughly well annealed to withstand sterilisation temperatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use robust, well-annealed glass to prevent breakage under vacuum/pressure and heat sterilisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glass type recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: All flasks should be either of Jena glass or Resistance (R) glass, the extra initial expense being justified by the comparative immunity of the glass from breakage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in higher-quality glassware for safety, longevity, and reduced laboratory hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petri dishes and capsule sizes and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Petri's dishes (plates) of 10 cm diameter and 1.5 cm height as standard; capsules in 4 cm x 2 cm and 5 cm x 2 cm sizes. Sterilise and store plates and capsules in cylindrical copper boxes with pull-off lids and internal stirrups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard sizes recommended for most work; storage in metal boxes facilitates sterilisation and aseptic removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduated pipette types and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep pipettes of 1 c.c. graduated in 0.1 c.c., 1 c.c. graduated in 0.01 c.c., and 10 c.c. graduated in 0.1 c.c.; pipettes should be ~30 cm long, the open mouth plugged with cotton-wool, sterilised and stored in separate cylindrical copper cases stamped with capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain separate storage for each capacity and sterilise before storage; long clear space above first graduation recommended for ease of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard (certified) graduated pipettes for calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a complete set of 'Standard' graduated pipettes, each stamped and authenticated by a recognised Physical Measurement Laboratory (e.g., Charlottenburg), including sizes from 10 c.c. down to 0.01 c.c.; reserve these for standardising ordinary pipettes and calibrating small laboratory-made pipettes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified standards should not be used for routine work but held for calibration to ensure volumetric accuracy across laboratory instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glass-working tools and skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential items for preparing glass apparatus in the lab: a three-square hard-steel file or glass-worker's knife for cutting glass tubes, a blowpipe flame (or Bunsen burner), and a bat's-wing burner; a foot-operated bellows-mounted blowpipe setup is recommended for convenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratory should be equipped and staff trained to make and modify small glass apparatus in-house for bespoke needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capillary (Pasteur) pipettes construction and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare capillary pipettes from soft-glass tubing (commonly 8 mm diameter), draw to form capillary portion, seal and round off ends, and plug with cotton-wool; filling/emptying by an unperforated rubber teat is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sterilise and store pipettes in metal cases or sealed test-tubes; variants with constrictions or longer capillary portions are useful for specific collections of morbid exudations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blood pipette design and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Blood pipettes made from soft glass tubing of 1 cm bore with a central bulb and terminal tubes at least 1 mm diameter to avoid capillary action; for sterilisation and storage each pipette is placed inside a test-tube resting on cotton-wool with a lance-headed pin or Hagedorn needle included so the entire outfit may be sterilised together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design avoids capillary-driven artefacts during blood collection; include lancet/needle in sterilisation kit to speed blood work setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduated capillary pipettes for minute volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Make small graduated capillary pipettes from manometer tubing, graduated (by standard pipettes) in hundredths to contain volumes such as 10, 50, 90 c.mm., and mark with a writing diamond; sterilise in large test-tubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for accurate percentage solutions when only minute fluid volumes are available; require careful calibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic ('throttle') pipettes—calibration & manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic throttle pipettes (Wright) made from capillary Pasteur pipettes and calibrated to deliver exact small volumes (e.g., 5 c.mm.); manufacture involves drawing capillary tips, loading known mercury volumes from a standard pipette, cutting and joining capillary and barrel portions, and sealing with wax to create an air-tight calibrated delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a reproducible small-volume pipetting method; stepwise calibration using standard pipettes is crucial for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fermentation/fermentation tubes and sedimentation tubes specs
rubrics_metrics.description: Fermentation tubes used for gas collection should be plain or graduated; sedimentation tubes (5 x 0.5 cm) and sedimentation pipettes made from narrow glass tubing (with sealed ends, bulbs, or constrictions) are used for small-quantity reactions and centrifugation in haematocrit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed by glassblowing techniques; small tubes can be mounted in plasticine blocks for stands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning new test-tubes protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: To clean new test-tubes: place in bucket, fill with water and soap powder, boil for 30 minutes (or autoclave similarly), brush interiors, rinse in cold water, invert to drain, dry and polish inside and out with a soft cloth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same cleaning applies to new flasks, plates, and capsules; ensures removal of manufacturing residues and grease before sterile use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning new graduated pipettes protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Place pipettes in soapy water, boil vigorously for 20 minutes, rinse in running water, run distilled water then rectified spirits through, then dry in hot-air oven by slowly raising to ~80°C or dry by blowing air through using bellows/blowpipe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of drying method (hot-air oven vs. blowing) depends on availability; ensures internal dryness and removal of residues without damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection & cleaning of infected test-tubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Pack infected tubes in autoclave basket vertical, remove plugs, fill each tube with water, disinfect by exposure to 120°C for 20 minutes in autoclave; if no autoclave, boil vigorously 30–45 minutes; while hot empty and clean with test-tube brush, boil in soapy water 30 minutes, acidulate in 2–5% hydrochloric acid for ~15 minutes, rinse and dry and polish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed contingency for absence of autoclave; sequences of thermal, mechanical, and chemical cleaning to ensure decontamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning flasks used for media preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Flasks used only in preparation of media must be cleaned immediately: fill with water with soap powder and a few crystals of potassium permanganate and boil; use flask brush; if needed, wash with 5% nitric acid or shake with cotton-wool rolled in silver sand, then rinse and polish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oxidising agents and mechanical abrasion recommended for stubborn residues from media preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning infected pipettes
rubrics_metrics.description: Plunge infected pipettes immediately after use into tall glass cylinders containing 2% lysol and allow to remain for some days; remove, drain, boil in soapy water for 30 minutes, rinse, immerse in 5% nitric acid for 1–2 hours, rinse in running water, then complete cleaning as for new pipettes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-stage chemical + thermal regimen recommended for heavily contaminated pipettes; long lysol soak facilitates subsequent cleaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid cleaning of blood/serum capillary pipettes using suction
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a Kitasato filter flask to a Sprengel suction or Geryk air pump, attach rubber tubing to draw distilled water, then rectified spirit, then ether through the pipette while pump operates; detach and dry in hot-air oven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suction-assisted cleaning accelerates removal of blood/serum residues from narrow capillary pipettes, saving time compared to repeated manual rinses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slides and cover-slips degreasing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopical slides and cover-slips when first purchased have 'greasy' surfaces which prevent spreading of thin, even films.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slides must be degreased (procedure follows in text) before use to ensure proper spreading and accurate microscopic preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sterile storage of glassware
rubrics_metrics.description: Glassware comprised in the laboratory list, in addition to being clean, must be stored in a sterile or germ-free condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After cleaning/sterilisation, ensure packaging/storage maintains sterility (e.g., sealed copper cases/boxes) until use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autoclave sterilisation parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Disinfect contaminated glassware by exposing to a temperature of 120 deg. C. for twenty minutes in the autoclave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If autoclave not available, use prolonged boiling (30–45 minutes) in a digester or pan with tightly fitting cover as an alternative.
